# USDC Circulation Decreases by 7 Billion in 7 Days, Total Supply at 74.8 Billion
GateNews
Capital Flow On-Chain Data
2026-06-14 01:39:48
USDC -0.03%
According to Circle official data, USDC circulation decreased by approximately 7 billion in the 7 days through June 11. Over the same period, Circle issued about 8.5 billion USDC while redeeming approximately 8.2 billion, resulting in a net outflow. Total USDC circulation stands at 74.8 billion.

# Circle reports $770 million Q4 revenue as USDC circulation reaches $75 billion, targets 40% CAGR for stablecoin
## Quick Take
- Circle reported Q4 revenue and reserve income of $770 million, a 77% increase from the prior year, as USDC in circulation rose to $75.3 billion.
- The company also issued multi-year guidance targeting a 40% compound annual growth rate for USDC in circulation.

...

The New York-based stablecoin issuer ended the year with $75.3 billion in USDC circulation, up 72% from the end of 2024.

...

Meanwhile, the company also issued multi-year guidance targeting a 40% compound annual growth rate for USDC in circulation. If sustained, that growth rate could significantly expand USDC’s share of the stablecoin market, currently led by Tether with roughly $183 billion in circulation, according to The Block’s [data dashboard](https://www.theblock.co/data/stablecoins/usd-pegged/total-stablecoin-supply).
[Expand Chart](https://www.theblock.co/data/stablecoins/usd-pegged/total-stablecoin-supply)

...

## Product expansion and digital asset growth
The company also provided updates on its Arc public testnet, which currently includes over 100 participants from the banking, capital markets, and technology sectors. According to the report, the testnet has processed more than 166 million total transactions with near 100% uptime and half-second finality. Daily average transaction volumes reached 2.3 million as of Feb. 20, 2026, with a mainnet launch scheduled for later this year.

## A Deep Dive on USDC
### USDC Token Fundamentals
#### Supply Characteristics
Unlike cryptocurrencies with fixed supplies, USDC follows a dynamic issuance model. New tokens are minted when users deposit U.S. dollars with a USDC issuer, and tokens are burned when redeemed for U.S. dollars. This creates a flexible supply that directly corresponds to user demand and dollar backing. There is no maximum supply cap, allowing the token supply to grow or contract based on market needs.
